name: inquiry-customer-goal
what_this_is: the frozen 72 resolution goals re-expressed as CustomerGoals (Inquiry v3.5 §4). It is NOT a new labelling of the corpus: the unit, the case set and the goal ids are the resolution gold's, and every row carries the frozen closing_authority it came from so the two can be compared row by row.
how_it_was_built: by a designer reading the 67 recorded customer messages (inquiry-planner-capture/v1) beside the frozen goals. NO MODEL CALL was made and none may be — a model labelling the set a Goal Interpreter will be scored against is the set measuring itself.
the_check: build.py asserts the new vocabulary is CONSISTENT with the frozen closing_authority under the deterministic ResolutionPolicy, reading its dispatch table backwards: INFORMATION->KNOWLEDGE, STATE_READ->ENTITY_STATE, ACTION->PROCEDURE, DECISION->KNOWLEDGE or SELLER. All 60 settled rows satisfy it and the build fails if any does not. This is falsifiable: a row labelled INFORMATION that closes on PROCEDURE means the label or the policy is wrong.
vocabulary_verdict: FOUR VALUES ARE ENOUGH. Zero of 72 goals need a fifth requested_outcome, and zero are unmappable. The 12 unsettled rows are not missing values: each is ambiguous about WHICH of the four it is, and those are product-owner decisions listed as six classes in labels.py ADJUDICATION and in docs/inquiry_architecture_v35.md §4.
the_finding_that_matters: 5 of the 7 PROCEDURE-closing goals in the whole frozen gold are adjudication rows. The DECISION/ACTION boundary the Resolution Planner kept crossing is a boundary this corpus never pinned down either, which is why no amount of prompt tuning closed it.
corpus_limitation: heavily INFORMATION (51 of 60 settled). STATE_READ has 3 settled rows and ACTION has 2. Layer A metrics computed on this set say almost nothing about STATE_READ or ACTION accuracy, and a targeted synthetic set carries that weight instead (contracts/inquiry-goal/v1/synthetic).
constraints_policy: explicit_constraints is stored as a COUNT in this dataset. The customer's actual words are not copied here and are not needed for any metric this dataset supports; constraint fidelity is scored against the recorded message in the capture, which never leaves the store.

label_policy.author: designer, 2026-09-20 (DEV/CALIBRATION — never a holdout)
label_policy.unit: one CustomerGoal per frozen resolution goal. The mapping is 1:1 BY CONSTRUCTION, which is itself a claim being tested: it asserts the smaller contract loses no goal the plan representation held.
label_policy.basis: STATED or DIRECTLY_IMPLIED. Exactly one row is DIRECTLY_IMPLIED (S:N8) and the line is drawn where an inference would authorise a side effect: inferring a QUESTION is cheap, inferring an ACTION is not — the four rows where the implied outcome is an action are adjudication class A, not settled.

derived_from.inquiry-planner-capture/v1: the 67 recorded customer messages at snapshot S0

holds: real inquiry id prefixes, designer labels and constraint COUNTS; no customer or seller text

storage.builder: contracts/inquiry-customer-goal/v1/build.py (committed; the labels it reads are not)
